                    ### Question
                    Which of the following drugs have properties similar to the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) ?:

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulates the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol. Tetracosactide, a synthetic derivative of ACTH, mimics its action and increases cortisol levels, confirming its similarity to ACTH. In contrast, Lanreotide and Pegvisomant do not have direct effects on adrenal function; Lanreotide primarily inhibits growth hormone and Pegvisomant blocks growth hormone receptors, neither of which relate to ACTH's role. Ganirelix, a GnRH antagonist, also does not influence adrenal cortex activity. Therefore, the only drug among the options that has properties similar to ACTH is Tetracosactide.
